requirements.requirement: Configure /srv/drop as a shared writable directory that prevents users from removing files owned by other users.
requirements.summary: The directory was created as root:root with mode 1777. Two unprivileged identities successfully created files, cross-owner deletion was denied in both directions, and the final directory was empty while retaining mode 1777. The behavior was also directly reconfirmed after restart with SELinux enforcing.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after observations consistently show RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. The implementation used installed standard system utilities, and the audit contains no package, release, or kernel modification.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete and coherent: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, reboot scheduling was acknowledged, connection loss and a different boot ID demonstrated the restart, and the running system, target, persisted probe, directory configuration, and access-control behavior all recovered. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with this transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and labeling /srv/drop was the required implementation. Temporary files used for behavioral and restart testing were bounded and removed. The reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol, and its transient unit disappeared with the reboot. Final observations show no failed services, new listeners, package-health regression, or executor test residue; temporary-file differences are normal regenerated systemd-private directories following the required reboot.
